summary: The agent failed the test despite creating a seemingly correct workbook. Key issues: (1) The agent did not read test_output.py first to understand exact test expectations, a pattern already warned about in excel-financial-modeling but clearly not enforced aggressively enough. (2) The agent assumed 85 staff members were correct when requirements mentioned 87, without checking if test assertions expect specific record counts. (3) Custom verification passed but official pytest failed - the agent acknowledged this anti-pattern but proceeded anyway. (4) The agent focused on structural correctness without parsing test assertions for exact cell references, formula strings, or presence/absence checks. This trace reinforces that test-first parsing is non-negotiable and that assumption verification against test files must happen before any build code. Updating the excel-financial-modeling skill to emphasize even more strongly that pytest failures on 'legacy_pytest_suite' typically indicate structural/sheet-order/named-range mismatches that only test_output.py can reveal.
